questions.question:
Let G be a connected undirected weighted graph. Consider the following two statements.

S1: There exists a minimum weight edge in G which is present in every minimum spanning tree of G.
S2: If every edge in G has distinct weight, then G has a unique minimum spanning tree.

Which one of the following options is correct?

options.A: Both S1 and S2 are true
options.B: S1 is true and S2 is false
options.C: S1 is false and S2 is true
options.D: Both S1 and S2 are false

questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- S1: if several edges share the minimum weight (e.g. a triangle with all weights 1), each MST leaves out one of them, so no single minimum edge is in every MST [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- S2: distinct weights [latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] unique MST [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: S1 is false and S2 is true

questions.question: Let H be a binary min-heap consisting of n elements implemented as an array. What is the worst case time complexity of an optimal algorithm to find the maximum element in H?
questions.explanation:
In a min-heap the maximum is in one of the [latex]\lceil n/2\rceil[/latex] leaves, and the leaves are not ordered among themselves, so all of them must be checked: [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex].

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex]

questions.question:
The format of the single-precision floating point representation of a real number as per the IEEE 754 standard is as follows:

[latex]\begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline \text{sign} & \text{exponent} & \text{mantissa} \\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]

Which one of the following choices is correct with respect to the smallest normalized positive number represented using the standard?
questions.explanation:
Normalized numbers need exponent field from 1 to 254 (0 is for zero/denormals). The smallest normalized positive number has exponent 00000001 and mantissa all 0: [latex]1.0\times2^{1-127}=2^{-126}[/latex].

Answer: exponent = 00000001 and mantissa = 0[latex]\ldots[/latex]0

questions.question: Consider the three-way handshake mechanism followed during TCP connection establishment between hosts P and Q. Let X and Y be two random 32-bit starting sequence numbers chosen by P and Q respectively. Suppose P sends a TCP connection request message to Q with a TCP segment having SYN bit =1, SEQ number =X, and ACK bit =0. Suppose Q accepts the connection request. Which one of the following choices represents the information present in the TCP segment header that is sent by Q to P?

options.A: SYN  bit =1, SEQ number =X+1, ACK bit =0, ACK number =Y, FIN bit =0
options.B: SYN  bit =0, SEQ number =X+1, ACK bit =0, ACK number =Y, FIN bit =1
options.C: SYN  bit =1, SEQ number =Y, ACK bit =1, ACK number =X+1, FIN bit =0
options.D: SYN  bit =1, SEQ number =Y, ACK bit =1, ACK number =X, FIN bit =0

questions.explanation:
Q's reply is the SYN-ACK:
- SYN = 1 with Q's own initial sequence number SEQ = Y
- ACK = 1, acknowledging P's SYN (which uses one number) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] ACK number = X + 1
- FIN = 0

Answer: SYN = 1, SEQ = Y, ACK = 1, ACK number = X+1, FIN = 0

questions.question: What is the worst-case number of arithmetic operations performed by recursive binary search on a sorted array of size n?

Each recursive call does a constant number of arithmetic operations (computing mid) and halves the range. The depth is [latex]\log_2 n[/latex], so the total is [latex]\Theta(\log_2 n)[/latex].

Answer: [latex]\Theta(\log_2(n))[/latex]

Consider the following sets, where [latex]n\geq 2[/latex]:

S1: Set of all nxn matrices with entries from the set [latex]\{a, b, c\}[/latex]
S2: Set of all functions from the set[latex]\{0,1,2,...,n^2-1\}[/latex] to the set [latex]\{0, 1, 2 \}[/latex]

Which of the following choice(s) is/are correct?

options.A: There does not exist a bijection from S1 to S2
options.B: There exists a surjection from S1 to S2
options.C: There exists a bijection from S1 to S2
options.D: There does not exist an injection from S1 to S2

- [latex]|S_2|=3^{n^2}[/latex] (each of the [latex]n^2[/latex] inputs has 3 choices).

- [latex](L_1\cap L_2)\cup(\overline{L_1}\cap L_2)=L_2[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CFL True

questions.question:
Choose the correct choice(s) regarding the following proportional logic assertion S:

[latex]S: (( P \wedge Q) \rightarrow R) \rightarrow (( P \wedge Q) \rightarrow (Q \rightarrow R))[/latex]

options.A: S  is neither a tautology nor a contradiction
options.D: The antecedent of S is logically equivalent to the consequent of S

So S has the form [latex]A\rightarrow A[/latex], which is always true.

Answer: S is a tautology; its antecedent is equivalent to its consequent

The value of |A-B| is _____________

A [latex]-[/latex] B = {R} [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] |A [latex]-[/latex] B| = 1

questions.question:
Consider the string abbccddeee. Each letter in the string must be assigned a binary code satisfying the following properties:

For any two letters, the code assigned to one letter must not be a prefix of the code assigned to the other letter.
For any two letters of the same frequency, the letter which occurs earlier in the dictionary order is assigned a code whose length is at most the length of the code assigned to the other letter.

Among the set of all binary code assignments which satisfy the above two properties, what is the minimum length of the encoded string?
questions.explanation:
Frequencies: a 1, b 2, c 2, d 2, e 3 (total 10).

Huffman: merge a(1) with a frequency-2 letter. To respect the tie rule (b, c, d in dictionary order), merge a with d [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 3; then b + c [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4; then ad + e [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 6; then 4 + 6.
Code lengths: a 3, d 3, b 2, c 2, e 2 (b [latex]\le[/latex] c [latex]\le[/latex] d True).

Length = 1[latex]\times[/latex]3 + 2[latex]\times[/latex]2 + 2[latex]\times[/latex]2 + 2[latex]\times[/latex]3 + 3[latex]\times[/latex]2 = 3 + 4 + 4 + 6 + 6 = 23

Answer: 23

questions.question:
Assume a two-level inclusive cache hierarchy, L1 and L2, where L2 is the larger of the two. Consider the following statements.

S1: Read misses in a write through L1 cache do not result in writebacks of dirty lines to the L2
S2: Write allocate policy must be used in conjunction with write through caches and no-write allocate policy is used with writeback caches.

Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: S1  is true and S2 is false
options.B: S1  is false and S2 is true
options.C: S1  is true and S2 is true
options.D: S1  is false and S2 is false

Checking each statement:
- S1: a write-through L1 never has dirty lines (every write already goes to L2), so a read miss never writes back a dirty line [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- S2: the usual pairing is the opposite (write-allocate with write-back, no-write-allocate with write-through), and neither is mandatory [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: S1 is true and S2 is false

questions.question:
Suppose we want to design a synchronous circuit that processes a string of 0's and 1's. Given a string, it produces another string by replacing the first 1 in any subsequence of consecutive 1's by a 0. Consider the following example.

[latex]\begin{array}{ll} \text{Input sequence:} & 00100011000011100 \\ \text{Output sequence:} & 00000001000001100 \end{array}[/latex]

A Mealy Machine is a state machine where both the next state and the output are functions of the present state and the current input.
The above mentioned circuit can be designed as a two-state Mealy machine. The states in the Mealy machine can be represented using Boolean values 0 and 1. We denote the current state, the next state, the next incoming bit, and the output bit of the Mealy machine by the variables s, t, b and y respectively.
Assume the initial state of the Mealy machine is 0.

What are the Boolean expressions corresponding to t and y in terms of s and b?
questions.explanation:
The state remembers the previous bit: t = b.

Output 1 only for a 1 that is not the first of a run, i.e. the current bit is 1 and the previous bit was 1: y = sb.

Check with 0011: outputs 0, 0, 0, 1 True

Answer: t = b, y = sb

questions.question:
Let S be the following schedule of operations of three transactions [latex]T_1, T_2 \text{ and }T_3[/latex] in a relational database system:

[latex]R_2(Y), R_1(X), R_3(Z), R_1(Y)W_1(X), R_2(Z), W_2(Y), R_3(X), W_3(Z)[/latex]

Consider the statements P and Q below:

P: S is conflict-serializable.
Q: If [latex]T_3[/latex] commits before [latex]T_1[/latex] finishes, then S is recoverable.

Which one of the following choices is correct?

options.A: Both P and Q are true
options.B: P is true and Q is false
options.C: P is false and Q is true
options.D: Both P and Q are false

questions.explanation:
Conflicts:
- [latex]R_1(Y)[/latex] before [latex]W_2(Y)[/latex]: T1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T2
- [latex]W_1(X)[/latex] before [latex]R_3(X)[/latex]: T1 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T3
- [latex]R_2(Z)[/latex] before [latex]W_3(Z)[/latex]: T2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] T3
No cycle [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] conflict serializable (T1, T2, T3). P is true.

T3 reads X written by T1. If T3 commits before T1, and T1 later aborts, T3 cannot be undone [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not recoverable. Q is false.

Answer: P is true and Q is false

questions.question: A bag has [latex]r[/latex] red balls and [latex]b[/latex] black balls. All balls are identical except for their colours. In a trial, a ball is randomly drawn from the bag, its colour is noted and the ball is placed back into the bag along with another ball of the same colour. Note that the number of balls in the bag will increase by one, after the trial. A sequence of four such trials is conducted. Which one of the following choices gives the probability of drawing a red ball in the fourth trial?
questions.explanation:
This is Polya's urn. By symmetry, every draw has the same chance of being red as the first draw.

Check for the 2nd draw: [latex]\frac{r}{r+b}\cdot\frac{r+1}{r+b+1}+\frac{b}{r+b}\cdot\frac{r}{r+b+1}=\frac{r(r+b+1)}{(r+b)(r+b+1)}=\frac{r}{r+b}[/latex]. The same holds for the 4th.

Answer: [latex]\frac{r}{r+b}[/latex]

questions.explanation:
Generator [latex]x^3+x+1[/latex] = 1011. Append 3 zeros: 11000000, then divide (XOR):

- 1110 [latex]\oplus[/latex] 1011 = 0101 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] bring 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 1010
- 1010 [latex]\oplus[/latex] 1011 = 0001 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] bring 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0010 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] bring 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 0100

Remainder = 100

Answer: 100

For a statement S in a program, in the context of liveness analysis, the following sets are defined:

questions.question:
For constants [latex]a\geq 1[/latex] and [latex]b \gt 1[/latex], consider the following recurrence defined on the non-negative integers:

Which one of the following options is correct about the recurrence [latex]T(n)[/latex]?

The others are wrong in general: e.g. option 1 fails for a = 4, b = 2 (gives [latex]\Theta(n^2)[/latex]), and case 2 has an extra log factor ([latex]\Theta(n^{\log_b a}\log n)[/latex]).

questions.question:
Consider a computer system with multiple shared resource types, with one instance per resource type. Each instance can be owned by only one process at a time. Owning and freeing of resources are done by holding a global lock (L). The following scheme is used to own a resource instance:
 function OWNRESOURCE(Resource R) 
    Acquire lock L // a global lock 
    if R is available then 
        Acquire R        
        Release lock L 
    else
        if R is owned by another process P then        
        Terminate P, after releasing all resources owned by P        
        Acquire R        
        Restart P        
        Release lock L        
        end if
    end if    
end function
Which of the following choice(s) about the above scheme is/are correct?

options.A: The scheme ensures that deadlocks will not occur
options.B: The scheme may lead to live-lock
options.C: The scheme may lead to starvation
options.D: The scheme violates the mutual exclusion property

questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- A process never waits while holding resources (the owner is terminated instead), so there is no circular wait [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] no deadlock.
- Two processes can keep terminating and restarting each other without progress [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] livelock possible.
- A process may be terminated again and again and never finish [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] starvation possible.
- Each resource still has only one owner at a time [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] mutual exclusion is kept.

Answer: Options 1, 2 and 3

questions.question:
Consider a computer network using the distance vector routing algorithm in its network layer. The partial topology of the network is shown below.

The objective is to find the shortest-cost path from the router R to routers P and Q. Assume that R does not initially know the shortest routes to P and Q. Assume that R has three neighboring routers denoted as X, Y and Z. During one iteration, R measures its distance to its neighbors X, Y, and Z as 3, 2 and 5, respectively. Router R gets routing vectors from its neighbors that indicate that the distance to router P from routers X, Y and Z are 7, 6 and 5, respectively. The routing vector also indicates that the distance to router Q from routers X, Y and Z are 4, 6 and 8 respectively. Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct with respect to the new routing table o R, after updation during this iteration?

options.A: The distance from R to P will be stored as 10
options.B: The distance from R to Q will be stored as 7
options.C: The next hop router for a packet from R to P is Y
options.D: The next hop router for a packet from R to Q is Z

questions.explanation:
Cost via each neighbour = (R to neighbour) + (neighbour's distance):
- To P: X 3 + 7 = 10, Y 2 + 6 = 8, Z 5 + 5 = 10 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 8 via Y
- To Q: X 3 + 4 = 7, Y 2 + 6 = 8, Z 5 + 8 = 13 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 7 via X

So R-P is 8 via Y (not 10), and R-Q is 7 via X (not via Z).

Answer: Distance to Q is 7; next hop to P is Y

Consider a three-level page table to translate a 39-bit virtual address to a physical address as shown below:

The page size is 4 KB = (1KB =[latex]2^{10}[/latex] bytes) and page table entry size at every level is 8 bytes. A process P is currently using 2 GB (1 GB =[latex]2^{30}[/latex] bytes) virtual memory which os mapped to 2 GB of physical memory. The minimum amount of memory required for the page table of P across all levels is _________ KB

2 GB / 4 KB = [latex]2^{19}[/latex] pages. Each page-table page holds 4096 / 8 = 512 = [latex]2^9[/latex] entries.

For the minimum, the pages are contiguous:
- Level 3: [latex]2^{19}/2^9=1024[/latex] pages
- Level 2: 1024 entries [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 2 pages
- Level 1: 1 page

Total = 1027 pages [latex]\times[/latex] 4 KB = 4108 KB

Answer: 4108

questions.question:
Consider a pipelined processor with 5 stages, Instruction Fetch(IF), Instruction Decode(ID), Execute (EX), Memory Access (MEM), and Write Back (WB). Each stage of the pipeline, except the EX stage, takes one cycle. Assume that the ID stage merely decodes the instruction and the register read is performed in the EX stage. The EX stage takes one cycle for ADD instruction and the register read is performed in the EX stage, The EX stage takes one cycle for ADD instruction and two cycles for MUL instruction. Ignore pipeline register latencies.
Consider the following sequence of 8 instructions:

ADD, MUL, ADD, MUL, ADD, MUL, ADD, MUL

Assume that every MUL instruction is data-dependent on the ADD instruction just before it and every ADD instruction (except the first ADD) is data-dependent on the MUL instruction just before it. The speedup defined as follows.

[latex]\textit{Speedup} = \dfrac{\text{Execution time without operand forwarding}}{\text{Execution time with operand forearding}}[/latex]

The Speedup achieved in executing the given instruction sequence on the pipelined processor (rounded to 2 decimal places) is _____________
questions.explanation:
Each instruction depends on the one before it. ADD uses EX for 1 cycle, MUL for 2.

With forwarding: the EX stages run back to back: 4 [latex]\times[/latex] (1 + 2) = 12 EX cycles from cycle 3 to 14, then MEM and WB [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 16 cycles.

Without forwarding: each instruction's EX (register read) waits until the previous one's WB. Each ADD/MUL pair then takes 1 + 2 EX cycles plus 2 waiting cycles (MEM, WB) each [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] the last WB is at cycle 30.

Speedup = 30 / 16 = 1.875 [latex]\approx[/latex] 1.87

Answer: 1.87
